chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz, from Ayub ibn Nuh, all together from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The divorce of the pregnant woman is one [pronouncement], and her waiting period is that she gives birth to her burden, and it is the closer of the two periods.'

key_terms.أَنْ تَضَعَ حَمْلَهَا: That she gives birth to her burden

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a pregnant woman who is divorced according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the iddah of a pregnant woman concludes upon childbirth, a ruling derived from the principle of selecting the shorter of the two potential waiting periods (menstruation vs. delivery). It highlights the juristic consensus in Shia fiqh that the physical act of giving birth serves as the definitive marker for the end of the marital bond, ensuring clarity in lineage and remarriage eligibility.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Abu Al Abbas Al Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, both together from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Divorce of the pregnant woman is once, and her term is that she places her load (gives birth), and it is the closest of the two terms (three menstruations or giving birth)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and abu al-‘Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayyub ibn Nuh all from Safwan from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Divorce of a pregnant woman is one and her waiting period is childbirth, if it is the nearer of the two.’”
